c1-3-001.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: The smoke alarm ___ off as soon as he ___ the candle underneath it. (go, light) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: The smoke alarm ___ off as soon as he ___ the candle underneath it. (go, light)
item.why: Two completed events that follow one another: past simple for both (*went off as soon as he lit*). The continuous would mean that one was in progress when the other happened.
item.why_lv: Divi *pabeigti* notikumi, kas seko viens *otram*: *abiem* Past Simple (*went off as soon as he lit*). Continuous forma nozīmētu, ka viens jau notika, kad notika *otrs*.

c1-3-002.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | We were flying to Oslo four times last year.

key.correct: We were flying to Oslo four times last year.
wrong: While my car was being repaired, I was cycling to work.
When the builders were here, I was making them tea all day.
She dropped her keys while she was getting out of the taxi.

item.why: With a count of repeated actions (*four times last year*), use the past simple: *We flew to Oslo four times.* The continuous is possible for repeated actions in a limited, temporary period (*While my car was being repaired, I was cycling*).
item.why_lv: Ja atkārtotas darbības *saskaita* (*four times last year*), lieto Past Simple: *We flew to Oslo four times.* Continuous forma iespējama atkārtotām darbībām īslaicīgā periodā (*While my car was being repaired, I was cycling*).
item.correct: We were flying to Oslo four times last year.
wrong: While my car was being repaired, I was cycling to work.
When the builders were here, I was making them tea all day.
She dropped her keys while she was getting out of the taxi.

c1-3-003.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | As soon as I saw her at the party, I was sure we ___ before. (meet) |

item.q: As soon as I saw her at the party, I was sure we ___ before. (meet)
item.why: *I was sure* is in the past, and the meeting was earlier still: past perfect, *we had met before* (not *we met*).
item.why_lv: *I was sure* ir pagātnē, un tikšanās bija vēl agrāk: Past Perfect, *we had met before* (nevis *we met*).

c1-3-004.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: I loved it. It was the best film I ___ ever ___. (see) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: I loved it. It was the best film I ___ ever ___. (see)
item.why: The film is compared with everything seen up to that past moment: *the best film I had ever seen* (past perfect).
item.why_lv: Filma *tiek* salīdzināta ar *visu*, kas redzēts līdz tam pagātnes brīdim: *the best film I had ever seen* (Past Perfect).

c1-3-005.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | We ___ each other for years before we started working together. (know) |

item.q: We ___ each other for years before we started working together. (know)
item.why: *know* is a state verb: past perfect simple, *had known*, not *had been knowing*.
item.why_lv: *know* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds: Past Perfect Simple, *had known*, nevis *had been knowing*.

c1-3-006.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | His voice was hoarse because he ___ all afternoon at the match. (shout) |

item.q: His voice was hoarse because he ___ all afternoon at the match. (shout)
item.why: The shouting was over and explains how his voice was later: past perfect continuous, *had been shouting* (not *was shouting*).
item.why_lv: Kliegšana jau bija *beigusies* un izskaidro, kāda vēlāk bija viņa *balss*: Past Perfect Continuous, *had been shouting* (nevis *was shouting*).

c1-3-007.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: When I got back to my desk, I could see that someone ___ my files. | had moved

item.q: Choose the correct option: When I got back to my desk, I could see that someone ___ my files.
item.why: A conclusion about something that happened before a past moment (*when I got back*): past perfect, *someone had moved my files*.
item.why_lv: Secinājums par to, kas notika pirms pagātnes brīža (*when I got back*): Past Perfect, *someone had moved my files*.

c1-3-008.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | These shoes are too small and the shop won't take them back. I wish I ___ the receipt. (keep) |

item.q: These shoes are too small and the shop won't take them back. I wish I ___ the receipt. (keep)
item.why: A regret about the past: *I wish* + past perfect, *I wish I had kept the receipt*. *I wish I kept* would be about the present.
item.why_lv: Nožēla par pagātni: *I wish* + Past Perfect, *I wish I had kept the receipt.* *I wish I kept* būtu par tagadni.

c1-3-009.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: My old flatmate ___ always ___ the lights on. It drove me mad. (leave) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: My old flatmate ___ always ___ the lights on. It drove me mad. (leave)
item.why: *was always* + *-ing*: a past habit that annoyed someone (*was always leaving the lights on*).
item.why_lv: *was always + -ing*: pagātnes ieradums, kas kādu kaitināja (*was always leaving the lights on*).

c1-3-010.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I had wondered if you could check my report.

key.correct: I had wondered if you could check my report.
wrong: I was wondering if you might have a minute.
I wanted to ask you about Friday.
We were hoping you could join us.

item.why: A polite request about now uses the past simple or continuous (*I was wondering if…, I wanted to ask…*), not the past perfect: *I had wondered* means that you wondered before some other past moment.
item.why_lv: Pieklājīgs lūgums par tagadni lieto Past Simple vai Continuous (*I was wondering if*…, *I wanted to ask*…), nevis Past Perfect: *I had wondered* nozīmē, ka domāji to pirms kāda cita pagātnes brīža.
item.correct: I had wondered if you could check my report.
wrong: I was wondering if you might have a minute.
I wanted to ask you about Friday.
We were hoping you could join us.
